inbox.title: Proposals
inbox.lede: Pages and edits Claude has drafted for this world. Nothing goes into the book until you accept it.
inbox.emptyBody: When Claude proposes a page or an edit through the Claude connection, it waits here for you.
inbox.emptyOff: The Claude connection is off. Turn it on in Settings to let Claude read this world and propose lore.
inbox.clearBody: Accepted and rejected proposals are removed from this list. Pages you accepted stay in the book.
inbox.homeNotice_one: Claude has proposed {{count}} change to this world.
inbox.homeNotice_other: Claude has proposed {{count}} changes to this world.

proposal.kindCreateHint: Claude proposes a page that does not exist yet
proposal.kindUpdateHint: Claude proposes a change to an existing page
proposal.conflictBody: Add this text, its stat-block values and aliases to that page, or give the new page another title.
proposal.pageGone: The page this edit was for no longer exists.
proposal.append: Text to add at the end

settings.title: Claude connection
settings.lede: Let Claude (Claude Desktop, Claude Code or another MCP client) read your worlds and propose new lore. A small bridge program runs on your computer and talks to this tab; your worlds stay in this browser.
settings.enableHint: Keep a Worldledger tab open while you work with Claude.
settings.addressHint: Change only if you started the bridge on another port.

state.connected: Connected. Claude can use this browser’s worlds.
state.unreachable: The bridge is not running. Start Claude with Worldledger set up (below), then wait a moment.
state.forbidden: The bridge refused this site. Add this address to WORLDLEDGER_ORIGINS (below).

settings.directHint: Off: every page and edit waits in the Proposals inbox until you accept it. On: they go into the book at once as drafts (and still appear in the inbox history). New pages whose title is taken always wait for you.
settings.setupLede: Do this once per computer. You need Node.js 18 or newer.
settings.step1: Download the bridge, a single file with no dependencies, and keep it somewhere permanent.
settings.pathHint: Fills in the path in the commands below. Stays in this browser.
settings.step2Desktop: Claude Desktop: open Settings → Developer → Edit Config and add this to claude_desktop_config.json, with the real path to the file. Then restart Claude Desktop.
settings.step2Code: Claude Code: run this in a terminal, with the real path to the file.
settings.step3: Turn on “Connect to Claude” above and ask Claude about your world, for example: “What does my world say about Varnhold? Draft the missing pages it links to.”
settings.originNote: This copy of Worldledger runs at {{origin}}, which the bridge does not allow by default, so the commands above set WORLDLEDGER_ORIGINS.
settings.privacy: Claude sees only what it asks for through the tools (a page, search results, related pages), and it can only propose. Nothing is sent anywhere except to the Claude app you connect.

warning.fields_not_object: The stat-block values were not in a form Worldledger understands, so none were applied.
warning.unknown_field: “{{field}}” is not a field of {{chapter}}, so it was left out.
warning.bad_value: {{value}} does not fit “{{field}}” ({{type}}), so it was left out.
warning.bad_date: {{field}}: {{value}} is not a year, so it was left out.
